title: Cold Expanded Hole Rework at a Cracked Fastener Location in Pressurised Shell Structure
abstract: Permanent repair scheme for a cracked fastener hole in pressurised shell structure using cold expansion and an interference fit fastener, with the fatigue credit that allows the location to be released from repeat inspection.

sections.purpose: Permanent repair of a cracked fastener hole in pressurised shell structure by cold expansion and interference fit fastener installation, within the declared diameter and edge distance limits.
sections.damage_assessment: The repair applies to a crack that has initiated at a fastener hole and has not extended beyond the allowable damage limit. The crack must be fully removed by the reaming operation; a crack that reaches the edge distance limit before it is removed is outside this scheme and requires a doubler repair. The reamed diameter must fall between 4.8 mm to 9.5 mm; a hole that finishes outside that range is rejected by this scheme. The assessment must establish the hole history from the aircraft structural repair record: a hole previously reamed oversize cannot be expanded, and a hole already expanded twice has reached its limit. Where the record is incomplete the hole is treated as unknown history and the repair is not applicable. Adjacent holes in the same row must be inspected before the repair, because a crack at one hole in a row of four is usually accompanied by a subsurface indication at its neighbour.
sections.repair_procedure: Remove the fastener and the surrounding protective treatment. Do the eddy current inspection to establish the crack length and confirm it is within the allowable damage limit. Ream the hole progressively until the crack is fully removed and confirm removal by eddy current at each increment. Measure the resulting diameter and confirm it is within the declared expansion range and that the edge distance is still above the minimum. Cold expand the hole using the mandrel and split sleeve for the measured diameter, drawing the mandrel through in one continuous stroke from the entry face given in the figure. Discard the split sleeve. Ream to the interference fit dimension for the fastener. Do the eddy current inspection of the expanded hole and record the result. Install the interference fit fastener EN824462K5 wet, using the sealing washer PE170760-37 where the hole passes through the pressure boundary. Where the local reinforcement is required, install the plate D5110113425482 with the clip D5110116963848 and the splice plate D5110118833865 as shown on repair drawing RD-51-10-11-001. Restore the protective treatment on both faces.
sections.inspection_requirements: Eddy current inspection of the expanded hole immediately after expansion and again after the fastener is installed. Where the local reinforcement is fitted, an additional inspection of the reinforcement fastener rows is required. The repeat inspection interval is the general structural sampling interval rather than the location-specific interval that applied before the repair, but only where the expansion is recorded in the aircraft structural repair record. An unrecorded expansion reverts the location to the pre-repair interval.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Cracks up to 6 mm measured from the hole edge, not closer than 12 mm to a free edge, and no more than one cracked hole in any four-hole group. The reamed diameter must be between 4.8 mm and 9.5 mm.

repair_drawings.title: Cold expanded hole with local reinforcement plate

type_data.fastener_pattern: Single expanded hole; where the reinforcement plate is fitted, two rows of eight fasteners at 18 mm pitch with 12 mm edge distance
type_data.fatigue_life_note: The expanded hole is credited with an improved fatigue detail and is released to the general structural sampling interval, provided the expansion is recorded. The credit does not apply to a hole with unknown history.
